summary: Create a board slice that owns cross-capability orchestration and policy. Work-items and labels expose typed server-side operations; neither imports the other. The RSC page calls one authenticated board read entrypoint that validates, reports, and returns a board-specific view model.

tree.purpose: Board filters, status groups, visible label details, and serializable board view-model types/schemas.
Coordinates work-item and label operations; hides archived items, groups by status, attaches visible labels, and rejects inaccessible label references.
Public application boundary: validates input/output, normalizes failures, and reports each failure once.
Server-only read adapter; verifies the actor/session, creates scoped dependencies, and invokes the board boundary.
Thin RSC route; calls the board read entrypoint and renders the returned view model or delegates classified errors to the route error surface.
Pure board presentation using grouped board data; no persistence or authorization logic.
Published work-items read operation; owns work-item persistence access and actor scoping.
Published labels read operation; owns label persistence access and actor visibility rules.
Work-item persistence adapter/module, returning domain-shaped work-item data.
Label persistence adapter/module, returning domain-shaped label data.

flows: GET/render /board: `src/app/board/page.tsx` -> `src/adapters/inbound/read/board/load-board.ts` -> verify server-derived actor/session -> `src/use-cases/board/entries/load-board.ts` -> `src/use-cases/board/operations/load-board.ts` -> `work-items.listBoardItems(actor, filters)` and `labels.listVisibleLabels(actor, referencedLabelIds)` -> board policy transformation -> validated board view model -> RSC renders `src/ui/board/BoardView.tsx`.

Board operation flow: fetch actor-scoped work items, remove archived items, collect referenced label IDs, fetch labels through the labels public operation, reject with `forbidden` if any referenced label is not visible, attach visible label details, then group remaining items by status.

Work-items flow: board operation -> published work-items operation -> `src/data/work-items/index.ts` -> work-item store/RLS. Labels follow the analogous path through `src/data/labels/index.ts`. Persistence and provider details remain inside their owning slices.

decisions.rationale: The combined projection and policies belong to the board, not to work-items or labels; this avoids duplicating policy and preserves independent changeability.

decisions.choice: Board may depend on published work-items and labels operations; work-items and labels must not depend on board or each other.
decisions.rationale: Cross-slice access uses operations-only public surfaces, keeping persistence and internals private.
It orchestrates two seams and creates a projection with board-specific rules, satisfying the use-case deletion test.

decisions.choice: Re-verify the actor in `adapters/inbound/read/board/load-board.ts` and preserve actor scope in both capability reads.
decisions.rationale: RSC rendering and proxy protection are not authorization boundaries; every protected read must authenticate server-side.

decisions.choice: Use the shared boundary taxonomy: `unauthorized`, `forbidden`, `upstream`, `network`, `contract`, or `unknown`.
decisions.rationale: The boundary reports once and the RSC adapter translates the classified result; raw database/provider errors never reach the UI.

decisions.choice: Fail the whole board read with `forbidden` when a non-archived item references a label the actor cannot view.
decisions.rationale: This explicitly enforces the requirement and prevents silently presenting an incomplete or misleading board.

decisions.choice: Use the RSC read path with no client cache unless realtime or shared client lifecycle is later required.
decisions.rationale: The board is a render-time read; RSC props are sufficient and keep cache ownership clear.

decisions.choice: Test board policy as an operation, boundary outcomes, capability data modules against the real local store, the inbound adapter with stubbed use-cases, UI rendering, and one authenticated e2e path.
decisions.rationale: Tests cross the same seams as production and assert outcomes rather than call mechanics.

risks: If existing work-items or labels APIs are only inbound declarations, add or expose typed server-side operations rather than having the board call one slice's boundary from another; declarations must not call declarations.

A label reference may be inaccessible because it is missing, unauthorized, or forbidden. Map the owning labels capability's policy result consistently to board-level `forbidden` without exposing provider details.

If the underlying store already performs grouping, archival filtering, or visibility transactions, keep that authority in the store and avoid reimplementing it; board should retain only genuinely board-specific composition and projection logic.
